title: "Coverage"

This page describes the published **v0.4.1** interfaces. Availability depends on
the election event, function, geographic level and counting stage. A supported
year does not imply that every combination exists. Function coverage indicates
which interfaces are available, not that every field, geographic level or
counting stage is available for each election.

## Data source views

`canonical`, `remote` and `local` describe how data are obtained:

- **Canonical:** the versioned set of validated Parquet files published in a
  swelections data release. These files provide a stable data basis for the
  published version without a local raw-data archive. They can also be read
  directly in other tools, such as Python.
- **Remote:** current data from an explicitly supported official source.
- **Local:** your own compatible saved source files, selected explicitly.

These source choices describe how data are obtained, not different degrees of
official status or quality, or the stage of the vote count.

## Counting stages

`final` and `preliminary` describe distinct stages of the official vote count.
Preliminary results are not simply incomplete final results. See
[Understanding Swedish elections](understanding-elections.html#electoral-geography)
for the role of election-night and collection counting.

The package uses only `"final"` and `"preliminary"` in `count_stage`; election
night and the collection count are not additional `count` choices. District
records separately identify `"ordinary"`, `"collection"` or `"wednesday"` in
`district_type`, following the source. Counting-stage availability varies by
election; a missing preliminary snapshot is never filled with final figures.

## Standard and full detail

`detail = "standard"` is the default output for most analyses. It includes the
main useful variables, with a structure kept as consistent as practical across
elections. `detail = "full"` adds information from the selected source, including
source-specific or technical fields. These additional fields can therefore vary
between elections and sources. Full output still follows the swelections table
structure; it is not an unchanged copy of the original raw file.

## Ordinary elections

The seven election-data functions are `results()`, `seats()`, `candidacies()`,
`candidates()`, `elected()`, `substitutes()` and `preference_votes()`.

| Election | Normal source | Function coverage | Result counting stages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Parliamentary (RD), regional (RF), municipal (KF), 2002 | Canonical | Six functions; no `candidacies()` | Final |
| RD/RF/KF, 2006 | Canonical | All seven | Final |
| RD/RF/KF, 2010 and 2014 | Canonical | All seven | Final and supported preliminary views |
| RD/RF/KF, 2018 | Canonical | All seven | Final; preliminary requests are rejected |
| RD/RF/KF, 2022 | Canonical | All seven | Final and supported preliminary views |
| RD/RF/KF, 2026 | Remote | Supported current functions and files | Availability follows the official current distribution |
| European Parliament, 2004, 2014 | Canonical | All seven | Final |
| European Parliament, 2009 | Canonical | Six functions; preference votes require explicit local sources | Final |
| European Parliament, 2019 and 2024 | Canonical | All seven | Final and supported preliminary views |
| Euro referendum, 2003 | Canonical | `results()` | Final |

Counting stages in this table refer to results. Candidate preference votes and
fixed elected/substitute relationships use their documented final-result
sources; they are not automatically available for every stage.

2022 election results are available through the published canonical data.
Separately supported current candidacy exports and 2022–2026 mandate-period
history are also available through remote sources. See `data_sources` for
function-specific source requirements.

## Geography

`results()` offers national, county/region, municipality, constituency and
voting-district views where applicable to the election and source. The
constituency categories include parliamentary, regional and municipal
constituencies; they are not interchangeable. See `results()` for exact
`level` values and `seats()` for mandate geography.

District output preserves ordinary and collection/Wednesday reporting units.
Collection votes are not artificially allocated to ordinary voting districts.
See [Understanding Swedish elections](understanding-elections.html#electoral-geography)
for constituencies, district codes, polling stations and collection districts.
Historical reporting structures can differ; source geography is retained rather
than harmonised across elections.

## Re-elections

These are separate election events within the original election's continuing
mandate period, rather than replacement ordinary elections in a time series.
All five have published canonical `results()` and `seats()`:

| Event | Geographic scope | Event seats |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Orsa, 16 March 2003 | Municipality 2034 | 31 |
| Västra Götaland, 15 May 2011 | Region 14 and its five constituencies | 149 |
| Örebro, 15 May 2011 | Nordöstra constituency 188004 only | 17 |
| Båstad, 10 May 2015 | Municipality 1278 | 41 |
| Falun, 7 April 2019 | Municipality 2080 | 61 |

Candidate-related functions are not enabled for these event products.
No complete preliminary re-election result is available.
Use `election_events()` or `valtillfallen()` to discover the events.

`seats(..., election_kind = "re_election")` returns the event allocation.
`seats(..., after_re_election = TRUE)` returns the verified effective composition
under the original ordinary election year. For Örebro this is 65 seats: 48
unaffected seats from 2010 plus 17 from the 2011 event. No new municipality-wide
seat allocation is calculated from combined votes.

## Mandate-period history

`mandate_history()`, `members_at()` and `vacant_seats_at()` use the same population
of allocated mandates. They describe formal electoral mandate holding under the
sources' date conventions, not attendance or temporary substitute service at
meetings.

- **2014–2018 and 2018–2022:** published canonical intervals, including Båstad and
  Falun re-election transitions within the original periods.
- **2022–2026:** current supported remote history/member files, not canonical
  history. Queries cannot extend beyond verified source-date coverage.
- **Earlier periods:** not included in the public mandate-history coverage.

For Båstad, the available source material does not allow holder continuity to be
verified from 15 September 2014 up to the 10 May 2015 re-election. Date-specific
queries requiring this interval return an error rather than inferring either a
continuing mandate or a vacancy.

## Important source limitations

- **RKL 2002:** the full ballot-candidacy population has not been recovered.
  Reported result/preference observations remain separate from that gap. Some
  small-party votes remain aggregated; missing original files do not imply
  missing final party totals where complementary official sources reconcile them.
- **EU 2009:** canonical preference votes are excluded because of unresolved
  source allocation and linkage issues. A compatible preserved archive can be
  used explicitly with `source = "local"`; auto never selects it. See the
  [detailed completeness record](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/blob/main/development/COMPLETENESS_EU_2009.md).
- **EU 2004:** 943 valid handwritten votes remain a reported aggregate without
  invented individual party designations.
- **EU 2014:** ten valid handwritten votes in Vårdsberg have an unreported party
  designation in the preserved result material; they remain in valid totals.
- **EU 2024:** candidate 1203 occurs in an earlier candidacy snapshot but is
  absent from the later approved population. This documented snapshot difference
  does not change the final votes or mandates.
- **Referendum 2003:** Blank is a valid voting option, separate from invalid
  ballots. Aggregate electorate composition is available nationally and by county:
  `eligible_swedish_citizens_in_sweden`, `eligible_swedish_citizens_abroad` and
  `eligible_foreign_citizens`. These sum to `eligible_voters`; they are missing
  at finer levels and are never allocated downward.

An unavailable complete preliminary collection snapshot is a source/recovery
limitation, not evidence that the authority never produced one. Election-night
material is not silently substituted for it.

See [Reference](../reference/index.html) for current interfaces and
[Sources & methodology](sources-methodology.html) for interpretation.
